written: 2026-11-14, from the challenge titles and one-line descriptions in the lab README, before any challenge server was started or its source read
method: Passive: handshake and tools/list only. A challenge is in scope when its weakness should be visible in what the server declares.

challenges.name: Basic Prompt Injection
challenges.why: The weakness is how user input is handled at call time.

challenges.name: Tool Poisoning
challenges.why: Hidden instructions sit in tool descriptions.

challenges.name: Excessive Permission Scope
challenges.why: An over-broad tool should be visible in its declaration.

challenges.name: Rug Pull Attack
challenges.why: The declaration changes only after tools are called, which a passive scan never does.

challenges.name: Tool Shadowing
challenges.why: Shadowing is normally carried by instructions in a description.

challenges.name: Indirect Prompt Injection
challenges.why: The payload arrives in data returned by a tool.

challenges.name: Token Theft
challenges.why: Tokens are exposed by calling tools, not by listing them.

challenges.name: Malicious Code Execution
challenges.why: A code-execution tool should be declared as such.

challenges.name: Remote Access Control
challenges.why: Command injection needs a tool that reaches a shell.

challenges.name: Multi-Vector Attack
challenges.why: At least one of the chained weaknesses should be declared.

challenges.name: JWT Claim Forgery
challenges.why: The secret leaks through tool output.

challenges.name: Hidden Identity Override
challenges.why: The parameter is undocumented, so it is absent from the declaration by construction.

challenges.name: Privilege Escalation via Workflow IDOR
challenges.why: An authorization flaw in server logic.

challenges.name: Marketplace Plugin Poisoning
challenges.why: The hidden instruction is in a plugin loaded at run time.

challenges.name: Dependency Confusion
challenges.why: The hidden instruction is in a package fetched at run time.
